title: Output-weight normalization and burst credit simulation for hosted per-token billing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Customers building generation-heavy features (summarization, codegen, explanation) have very high output token counts and perceive per-token billing as unpredictable compared to more balanced input/output workloads. We want to test two related pricing interventions: 1) apply an output-weight normalization factor that reduces effective billed weight for long-output responses based on task category; 2) introduce short-term burst credits (a smoothing buffer) that absorb occasional output spikes without triggering minimums or large bill jumps. The goal is to reduce billing variance for common enterprise patterns while preserving unit economics.
hypothesis: Applying an output normalizer (tiered multiplier that decays after X tokens) will reduce per-customer billing variance by >=25% for long-output workloads without increasing average cost per token by more than 5%.

Burst credits (a rolling 1-hour token buffer per customer that discounts the first N oversized responses) will lower support escalations and churn signals for customers hitting short-lived output spikes.
Combining normalization + burst credits will increase perceived billing fairness in qualitative interviews and improve NPS for PLG signups doing heavy generation demos.
success_metrics: Billing variance (weekly per-customer coefficient of variation) decrease >=25% for cohort A
Change in 30-day ARR impact: uplift or neutral (delta <= +5% cost to Redwood)
Support tickets referencing "billing surprise" reduced by 40% for test cohort
Retention: churn in month following experiment <= control
Latency and SLOs unaffected: p95 token latency delta <= 3%
experiment_design: Cohorts: 10% exposed (stratified by avg output tokens), 10% control, remainder baseline logging only
Normalization rule: output_weight = max(1.0, 1.0 - 0.15 * floor((tokens_out - 512)/512)) with floor caps at token bands (512, 1024, 2048)
Burst credit rule: per-customer rolling 60-minute buffer; first 10k output tokens per hour discounted by 50% applied at bill run
Duration: 4 weeks with continuous telemetry; first 2 weeks focused on safety and observability checks
Billing treatment: visible invoice line item labeled 'Burst credit / Output normalization (pilot)'; partners/enterprises opted-in via contract flag
telemetry_queries: billing_weekly_variance_by_customer_v2: SELECT customer_id, STDDEV(total_tokens)/AVG(total_tokens) AS cov FROM billing_tokens_weekly WHERE cohort IN ('test','control') GROUP BY customer_id
support_tag_query: filter tickets where subject ~ 'billing' AND text ~ 'surprise' OR 'spike'
latency_impact_report: dashboard p50/p95 token generation latency by model and cohort
invoice_sample_check: list invoices with pilot line items and compute per-invoice delta vs baseline
rollout_plan: Step 0: Finalize formula + legal language for pilot customers (PM + Legal)
Step 1 (Canary): 1% traffic for 48 hours; daily review of telemetry and billing anomalies
Step 2 (Scale): 10% for 14 days; weekly stakeholder sync; enable auto-rollback if >10% customers see >20% bill delta
Step 3 (Enterprise opt-in): Offer pilot flag for selected enterprise accounts; collect contract feedback
Step 4: Decide: kill, iterate, or expand to GA and prepare pricing docs
risks_mitigations: Risk: Unexpected revenue leakage if normalization applied too aggressively. Mitigation: conservative formula, billing caps, daily revenue delta alerting
Risk: Customer confusion about invoices. Mitigation: explicit invoice line item and proactive comms + support playbook
Risk: Fraud/vector abuse by gaming burst buffer. Mitigation: fraud detection rules, per-account rate limits, and post-hoc reconciliations
